one_liner: Rust/Wasm fine-grained-reactive UI library; its 2023 beta ran the keyed DOM benchmark about 1.4x faster than React 19.2 hooks.
what_it_does: Sycamore builds browser UIs in Rust compiled to WebAssembly, with Solid-style signals, memos and effects instead of a virtual DOM. Components are plain functions returning View, written with the view! macro or the builder API (div().class(..).children(..)); the same code renders on the server (SSR, streaming SSR) and can hydrate in the browser. It replaces React or another JS framework wholesale; nothing about it is drop-in.
how_it_is_fast: Fine-grained reactivity: each signal knows its dependents, so an update re-runs only the effect bound to one text node or attribute, with no virtual-DOM diff (the reactive graph lives in a slotmap under one Root, 'Reactivity v3'). Keyed lists are reconciled with a udomdiff-style prefix/suffix/swap-backwards/map algorithm (reconcile_fragments), which is why swapping two rows costs 13.1 ms against React's 89.7 ms. The measured 0.9.0-beta.2 build also cloned cached <template> elements to create rows; the current 0.9.x code creates each element with document.createElement, using wasm-bindgen string interning (default feature) to cut JS string crossings.
when_to_use: A team that wants to write the whole front end in Rust and share types and logic with a Rust backend
List-heavy UIs with reordering (swap, move) where React's keyed reconciliation is slow: swap 1,000 rows 13.1 ms vs 89.7 ms in the suite
Large table creation: create 10,000 rows 263.7 ms vs React 401.0 ms, and lower run memory (2.10 vs 4.37 MB) in the suite
Apps that need SSR with streaming and hydration from the same component code
Developers who like SolidJS's model and want it in Rust with Copy, 'static signals and no lifetime parameters
when_not_to_use: If raw DOM speed is the goal: the suite has it at 1.296x vanilla JS's time and behind Solid 1.9.3, Silkenweb, Leptos 0.7.0, rust-dominator and Dioxus 0.7.2 (derived from page data)
Small create-heavy pages: create 1,000 rows is 24.8 ms vs React's 23.6 ms, and ready memory is higher (1.68 vs 1.19 MB)
Sites with a strict Content-Security-Policy: the suite flags the implementation with issue #1139 (does not pass strict CSP), as for most Wasm-instantiating builds
When the published numbers must describe the version you ship: they come from a 2023 beta whose rendering path no longer exists
Teams needing a large ecosystem or many maintainers: development is mostly one maintainer, and the README itself points to Leptos's larger community

integration.dependencies: wasm-bindgen, web-sys, js-sys, slotmap, smallvec, once_cell, paste and the sycamore-* sub-crates; optional futures/serde for suspense and serde features
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.94 (MSRV raised in 0.9.3), edition 2024; wasm32-unknown-unknown target plus Trunk or wasm-pack for browser builds
integration.platforms: Browsers via wasm32-unknown-unknown (DOM backend); any native target for SSR (selected by target arch, or --cfg sycamore_force_ssr for server-side Wasm)
integration.thread_safety: Single-threaded: the reactive Root is a thread-local global and signals are not Send; SSR's render_to_string keeps one root per thread

gotchas: Measured code path is gone: the suite's sycamore-v0.9.0-beta.2 bundle (prebuilt 2023-10) creates rows by cloning cached <template> content (the beta.2 view! macro emits a static Template per element root, instantiated from TEMPLATE_CACHE in dom_node_template.rs), while View v2 in 0.9.0 removed GenericNode/Html and the 0.9.4 sources build each element with document.createElement; nobody has published js-framework-benchmark numbers for 0.9.x, although the in-repo examples/js-framework-benchmark is already ported to the 0.9 API.

Bugs fixed after the measured beta: Keyed/Indexed wrong node order (#795, map index i instead of b_start+i, fixed in PR #796, 2025-04), dead dependents piling up after disposing memos (PR #831, 0.9.3) and event callbacks firing after drop ('closure invoked recursively or destroyed', #433, fixed by PR #837 in 0.9.4). Tracing the beta.2 reconcile_fragments shows the suite's swap, remove, append and replace-all operations take the prefix/suffix/swap paths or reach the map path with b_start 0, so the measured rows did not hit the #795 bug.

No event delegation (issue #176 open since 2021): every on:click is its own wasm-bindgen Closure plus addEventListener (dom_node.rs), so each benchmark row allocates two closures; the suite does not isolate this cost, but it is extra per-row work that delegating JS frameworks avoid.

create_root leaks its Root struct by design (Box::leak, documented 'lives until the end of the program'); code that creates a fresh root per request or per test grows memory, while render_to_string reuses a thread-local root.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: In the same Chrome 154 snapshot the keyed Rust entries rank, as geometric-mean fraction of React 19.2's time: hand-written wasm-bindgen 0.584, Silkenweb 0.622, rust-dominator 0.681, Leptos 0.684, Dioxus 0.698, Sycamore 0.711, Yew 0.819, ElementaryUI 0.877 (derived from page data), so pick Sycamore for its Solid-like API, SSR streaming and small bundle rather than for speed; pick Leptos or Silkenweb if suite speed decides it.
verified_claims_summary: Independent krausest/js-framework-benchmark snapshot (Chrome 154, MacBook Pro 14 M4 14/20 cores, OSX 26.6.2, 15 runs per test): the prebuilt sycamore 0.9.0-beta.2 keyed bundle (lto, codegen-units 1, wasm-opt -O4; rustc version not stated) takes 0.711x React 19.2 hooks' median total time over 9 CPU tests (about 1.41x faster) but 1.296x vanilla JS's time; the gain is mostly swap rows (13.1 vs 89.7 ms) and 10k creation (263.7 vs 401.0 ms) (derived from page data, recomputed this session from results.ts).
status_note: Active and MIT-licensed (0.9.4 released 2026-10-06, about 313k crates.io downloads), usable today for Rust front ends, but the only independent speed numbers describe a 2023 beta with a since-removed template-cloning renderer, so current performance is unmeasured.
